content.text: USER-APPROVED CORRECTION (2026-11-06): horizontal XDS SubNavigation replaces the earlier collapsible-section requirement. As a settings user, I want to switch between AI Models, Organization capabilities and Submission contract references using the standard horizontal navigation, so I can focus on one settings area while preserving unsaved work. Acceptance: AI Models initially active; exactly one visible panel; lazy initial loading; retain drafts, scope, selected model and notices after navigating away/back; keyboard and mobile support; actual records and explicit defaults only; existing permissions/payloads unchanged; executable fixture and API-backed regression evidence. Earlier accordion-specific criteria are superseded.
User request (2026-11-06): separate Settings into subsections using the standard XDS section component.

User story: As an individual or organization administrator, I want clearly labeled, independently expandable settings subsections so I can find and manage the relevant configuration without scrolling through unrelated forms. Reuse the existing settings workflows and AIN-138 user story; this task supplements AIN-140 and does not replace its broader obligations.

Scope / source map: EnsuredUI/src/Pages/InsurerDashboard/Settings.tsx currently renders ModelLibrary, OrganizationCapabilitiesSettings and SubmissionReferenceSettings consecutively. Reuse the exported XDS CollapsibleSection from EnsuredXDS/src/components/CollapsibleSection.tsx (already used in SubjectInsuranceSection and SubjectTemplateFields). Use XDS tokens and its controlled collapsed/onToggle API; do not build a parallel custom accordion. SectionHeader is a heading primitive, not a substitute for the standard section container.
Acceptance criteria:

Settings has three clearly labeled subsections: AI Models, Organization capabilities, and Submission contract references. Each uses the standard XDS CollapsibleSection with concise descriptive text and consistent spacing, headings and responsive styling.

Sections expand/collapse independently via pointer and keyboard, expose correct aria-expanded state, and have visible focus. Avoid duplicate page-level titles or nested action buttons inside the section toggle. Keep all existing workflows reachable.

Collapse/reopen preserves unsaved drafts, selected records, scope and relevant status. Current CollapsibleSection unmounts children when collapsed: explicitly solve state preservation by lifting state or a backward-compatible shared component enhancement; do not lose API keys being entered or trigger accidental saves/tests. Initial open/closed state is deliberate and covered by tests.

Preserve permissions and all current save/test/default/inheritance/removal behavior. Show only actual saved model records; do not seed providers or choose unknown defaults. No backend configuration, credential, authorization or data-model changes required for presentation regrouping.

Executable Storybook play stories cover section toggling, independent state, keyboard/focus, draft preservation, observable save results and exact submitted payloads; include loading, empty, error/retry, permission and narrow-screen states. Use synthetic transports and block accidental application writes. Retain existing component and API/database regressions. If XDS changes, add shared-component regressions.
Verify the integrated Settings page at desktop and 375px without horizontal overflow; record ticket -> component -> story IDs -> commands/results in Jira and TASK_HANDOFF.md before Done.

Related work: AIN-138 / AIN-140 own model settings behavior; AIN-143 chat connection behavior must not regress. Existing provider-access/staging gates remain open and are not prerequisites for arranging the settings sections. Exclude new providers, financial workflows, unrelated settings features and production rollout.
Implementation and local verification complete on 2026-11-06; see completion evidence comment. Broader linked outcomes remain open.

fields.summary: [Persona] Review document-generated forms with complete evidence and safe extensions

content.text: User story

As a underwriter, broker or reinsurer, I want to review structured forms generated by the LLM from supplied documentation so that unfamiliar risks remain reviewable without invented facts or a rigid universal form.
Feedback coverage
Original feedback: I5, B2, B3, R1, R2. I = insurer; B = broker; R = reinsurer; numbering follows the 20 points per persona in the user conversation.
Scope and existing implementation

Extend current services, generated-form workbench, commercial records and tests. These are outcome/verification gaps, not an assertion that every underlying capability is absent. Preserve existing working functionality and all broader parent obligations.
Existing implementation owners: AIN-15, AIN-16, AIN-50. Existing tasks retain their original scope and hierarchy. Completed tasks are reuse evidence, not proof that this broader story is Done.
Acceptance criteria
1. Generate sections and repeated entities from the documented evidence; preserve unknown extensions rather than discard fields outside a fixed template.
2. Each populated field exposes document/version/page or table-cell anchors, semantic binding, entity identity, unit/currency and unresolved/conflicting state; missing facts are not zero.

3. Validate candidate schemas and component references deterministically against the approved XDS registry; unsupported components render safely with visible diagnostics and cannot execute generated code.
4. Treat documents as data, including embedded instructions; invalid output, provider timeout or partial generation leaves the current effective form intact and offers bounded retry.
Required dependencies
Required predecessor outcomes: No new-story predecessor; use the existing implementation contracts/tasks listed above.; final Jira key mapping follows below.
Story-specific verification

Run scanned-document, table, sparse, conflicting, unfamiliar-class, repeated-entity and hostile-instruction cases; assert retained facts and exact submitted semantic payloads. Record a configured-provider evaluation separately from deterministic fixtures.
Definition of Done

1. All acceptance criteria and the story-specific verification scenario pass; link implementation tasks/PRs and record the reviewed source/package versions. A partial component or newly created ticket does not satisfy this story.

2. Every changed UI workflow has executable Storybook play functions asserting user actions, observable results and exact submitted payloads, including success, validation, failure/retry, empty/loading, pagination and permission/revocation states where applicable. Document a reason for any nonapplicable state. Include keyboard and narrow-screen checks.

3. Fixture stories use isolated synthetic transports with accidental application writes blocked. Also run authenticated real-service journeys against isolated Docker databases/services for authorization, durable state, concurrency, idempotency and relevant money invariants. Backend-only work uses integration evidence linked to this story, not artificial UI.

4. Attach ticket → component → Storybook story IDs → command/results mapping, regression evidence, API/database checks and known coverage gaps to Jira and TASK_HANDOFF.md. New failures have linked bug tickets and regressions; no unresolved failure of an acceptance criterion permits Done.

5. Reconcile all required dependencies and subtasks. Record migration/backfill compatibility and rollback results when schemas change. Demonstrate the workflow in the integrated staging environment, identifying deployed build and service versions; local checks alone are not staging evidence. Production deployment remains a separate release gate under AIN-1/12.

6. For external-system or monetary settlement claims, attach configured vendor/provider-sandbox evidence and matched reconciliation; simulated events or manually recorded receipts cannot establish external delivery or settled cash.

Generated-form gate: preserve document-driven extensibility, evidence anchors, stable semantic/entity IDs, missing/conflicting states and human corrections; pin schema/catalog/generator versions, reject unsafe generated structures and prove regeneration/replay behavior. LLM output never independently grants authority, approves coverage, sets eligibility or posts money.
Completion boundary
Backlog planning only on 2026-11-04. No implementation, test execution, migration or deployment is claimed. Assignee, estimates and dates remain for delivery planning.
Resolved delivery map — persona feedback 2026-11-04
Implementation ownership

Required implementation tasks/slices: AIN-15, AIN-16, AIN-50. Reuse existing completed work, implement and verify the remaining acceptance criteria in this story. Relates links identify shared ownership; Blocks links identify ordered predecessor outcomes.
Predecessor stories
No additional predecessor stories.
Verification mapping

Before Done, replace the pending evidence with actual component paths, Storybook story IDs, execution commands/results, Docker integration evidence and staging build IDs. Evidence is currently NOT RUN; no synthetic result is claimed.
Single-developer sprint sequence — 2026-11-04
Target candidate: AIN S10 | Document-generated review forms (Jira sprint 45).
Sprint outcome: Deliver reviewable LLM-generated structured forms on pinned evidence and validated component contracts.
Exit evidence: Sparse/conflicting/unfamiliar/repeated/hostile-document corpus passes; extensions and evidence survive; unsafe output and provider failures cannot replace the active form.

Planning envelope: 6 implementation days + 2 integrated verification days + 1 review/refinement day + 1 contingency day; not measured velocity. One primary outcome in progress; at most two closely related workflow slices. Story/task pairs share effort, not double-counted work.

Existing active sprint remains active with original dates; only its goal/name and unfinished membership are reorganized. Every new sprint is future and undated. No fabricated story-point/time estimates or assignees. The ordered slots are a provisional work breakdown, not a fixed delivery forecast. Before activation, split any candidate exceeding six implementation days and verify reviewer/provider readiness; preserve all parent acceptance criteria.

Scheduling is not implementation: original AC/DoD and parent scope are unchanged. Related story/task/subtask effort is one delivery slice, not additive capacity. Required domain slices can be delivered earlier than the broader owner completion sprint; no broader item is Done until all original requirements pass.
